      =\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{i}^{2}-2t\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{i}b_{i}+t^{2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}b_{i}^{2}.

      -2\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{i}b_{i}\bigr)t
      +\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{i}^{2}\bigr).
\]

A quadratic polynomial \(At^{2}+Bt+C\) with \(A>0\) is non‑negative for all
real \(t\) iff its discriminant is non‑positive:

\[
\Delta = B^{2}-4AC\le 0 .
\]

\[

C=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{i}^{2}.

              -\bigl(\sum a_{i}^{2}\bigr)\bigl(\sum b_{i}^{2}\bigr)\Bigr]\le 0 .
\]

\[
\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{i}b_{i}\bigr)^{2}
\le\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{i}^{2}\bigr)\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{n}b_{i}^{2}\bigr).

A function \(f:\mathbb {R}\rightarrow\mathbb {R}\) is **convex** iff for every
\(t\in[0,1]\) and every \(x,y\in\mathbb {R}\),

\[
f\bigl(tx+(1-t)y\bigr)\le t\,f(x)+(1-t)\,f(y). \tag{1}
\]

We prove Jensen’s inequality  

\[
f\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda _i x_i\right)\le\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda _i f(x_i)
\tag{J}
\]

### Base case \(n=1\)

If \(n=1\) then \(\lambda _1=1\) and (J) reduces to the identity  
\(f(x_1)\le f(x_1)\), which is true.

---

### Base case \(n=2\)

When \(n=2\) the statement is exactly (1) with \(t=\lambda _1\) and
\(1-t=\lambda _2\). Hence (J) holds for two points.

---

Assume (J) holds for any collection of \(k\) points with non‑negative
weights summing to 1, where \(k\ge 2\).
Consider a collection of \(k+1\) points \(\{x_1,\dots ,x_{k+1}\}\) with
weights \(\{\lambda _1,\dots ,\lambda _{k+1}\}\).

If one of the weights is zero, the inequality reduces to the case of
\(k\) points, which holds by the induction hypothesis.  
Thus we may assume every \(\lambda_i>0\).

Define  

\[

\qquad
\alpha_i=\frac{\lambda_i}{\mu}\;(i=1,\dots ,k).
\]

The numbers \(\alpha_i\) are non‑negative and satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^{k}\alpha_i=1\).

Let  

\[

\]

Now write the weighted average of all \(k+1\) points as a convex

\[

\]

Apply the convexity inequality (1) to the pair \((y,x_{k+1})\) with
parameter \(\mu\):

\[

By the induction hypothesis applied to the \(k\) points

\[

    \le\sum_{i=1}^{k}\alpha_i f(x_i). \tag{4}
\]

Multiply (4) by \(\mu\) and substitute into (3):

\[
\begin{aligned}
f\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{k+1}\lambda_i x_i\right)
&\le \mu\sum_{i=1}^{k}\alpha_i f(x_i)+(1-\mu)f(x_{k+1})\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i f(x_i)+\lambda_{k+1}f(x_{k+1}),
\end{aligned}
\]

because \(\mu\alpha_i=\lambda_i\) and \(1-\mu=\lambda_{k+1}\).

Thus (J) holds for \(k+1\) points. By induction, Jensen’s inequality is
true for every integer \(n\ge 1\).

Define a probability measure that places mass \(\lambda_i\) at the point
\(x_i\). Convexity of \(f\) is equivalent to the statement that for any
two points \(a,b\) and any \(t\in[0,1]\),

\[

\]

\[
f\!\left(\int x\,d\lambda\right)\le\int f(x)\,d\lambda,
\]

which, in the discrete case, is precisely

\[
f\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_i x_i\right)\le
\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_i f(x_i).
\]

Hence the desired inequality is proved.

∎
